title: Periodization Theory: Confronting an Inconvenient Truth
findings: Periodization theory has emerged over seven decades as the preeminent training planning paradigm, with its philosophical assumptions largely unchallenged.
The theory is repeatedly tied to Selye's stress research and the assumption that mechanical training stress directly regulates the magnitude of subsequent fitness adaptation.
Since then the science of stress has evolved extensively; the author argues for re-evaluating periodization and realigning it with contemporary stress theory.
limitations: Conceptual argument with no new data or numeric guidance; no specific alternative model proposed in the abstract.
implications: Treat any fixed periodization template as a prior to be adapted by observed response; re-plan from recent data rather than locking a season calendar.
No parameter change is justified; use as rationale for data-responsive rather than fixed recovery weeks.

verification.notes: Crossref issued 2017 (online); Sports Med 2018;48(4):753-764 per PubMed, so 2018 retained. Abstract verified from PubMed.
